item.title: Nhibernate Join Queryover
item.author: Author
item.description: When working with NHibernate and QueryOver, you can join multiple tables using the JoinAlias method. Let’s say you have the following entities: Person, PersonFavorites, PersonCompany, and Company. You want to join them based on their relationships. Here’s an example of how to do that: Define your entities (similar to the previous example): public class Person { public virtual int Id { get; set; } public virtual ICollection<PersonFavorites> Favorites { get; set; } public virtual ICollection<PersonCompany> Companies { get; set; } } public class PersonFavorites { public virtual Person Person { get; set; } public virtual Favorite Favorite { get; set; } } public class PersonCompany { public virtual Person Person { get; set; } public virtual Company Company { get; set; } } public class Company { public virtual int Id { get; set; } // Other properties.

item.title: MSSQL - Indexes
item.author: Author
item.description: In Microsoft SQL Server, an index is a data structure that is used to improve the performance of queries by providing faster access to the data in a table. An index allows the database engine to quickly locate the rows in a table that match a particular search condition, rather than having to scan the entire table. There are several types of indexes in SQL Server, including: Clustered index A clustered index determines the physical order of the rows in a table and can only be created on one column per table.

item.title: MSSQL - Execution Plan
item.author: Rob
item.description: General Information An execution plan in Microsoft SQL Server is a set of steps that the database engine follows to execute a SQL query. Execution plans are used by the database engine to determine the most efficient way to execute a query and can be used to troubleshoot performance issues. There are two types of execution plans in SQL Server: Estimated execution plan: An estimated execution plan is a graphical representation of the steps that the database engine estimates it will take to execute a query.

item.title: C# - Exceptions
item.author: Author
item.description: In C#, an exception is an object that represents an error that occurs during the execution of a program. Exceptions are used to signal that an error has occurred and to provide information about the error. Exceptions in C# are represented by classes that derive from the System.Exception class. When an error occurs in a C# program, an exception object is created and thrown. The exception can then be caught and handled by the program.

item.title: C# - Collections
item.author: Rob
item.description: General Information In C#, a collection is a group of objects that can be iterated over and manipulated as a single unit. There are several built-in collection types in C#, as well as many third-party libraries that provide additional collection types. Here is a list of the built-in collection types in C#: Array: An array is a fixed-size collection of items of a particular type. It provides fast random access to items, but slower insertion and removal of items.

item.title: C# - Entity Framework
item.author: Rob
item.description: Entity Framework General Concepts Entity Framework is an object-relational mapper (ORM) that enables .NET developers to work with a database using domain-specific objects. It eliminates the need for most of the data-access code that developers usually need to write. Here’s a high-level overview of how Entity Framework works: You design your domain model classes in your .NET application, with each class representing a table in your database. You use Entity Framework to create a mapping between your domain model classes and the corresponding tables in the database.

item.title: C# - Boxing Unboxing
item.author: Author
item.description: Boxing and unboxing are two important concepts in C# that allow you to convert between value types and reference types. Boxing is the process of converting a value type to a reference type. For example, you might want to store a value of an integer type in a variable of type object. To do this, you would need to box the integer value so that it can be stored in the object variable.

item.title: Home Server - Fedora Linux
item.author: Author
item.description: How to How to install, start and connect to SSH Server on Fedora Linux $ sudo systemctl status sshd # if inactive... $ sudo systemctl enable sshd $ sudo systemctl start sshd # now should be active # try to connect from other machine.. $ ssh [remote_user_name]@x.x.x.x How to install docker-compose $ sudo curl -L "https://github.com/docker/compose/releases/download/1.26.0/docker-compose-$(uname -s)-$(uname -m)" -o /usr/local/bin/docker-compose $ sudo mv /usr/local/bin/docker-compose /usr/bin/docker-compose $ sudo chmod +x /usr/bin/docker-compose Start PiHole $ docker-compose up -d Issues Cannot connect to docker daemon # check status $ sudo service docker status # if not running then.
